description:
4‑in‑1 65W fast charging cable is the one travel cable that replaces the mess of different wires in your bag. With dual inputs (USB‑C and USB‑A) and dual outputs (USB‑C and Lightning), it lets you charge iPhone and Android devices, iPad, power banks, and even compatible USB‑C laptops using the charger you already have. Plug into a USB‑C PD adapter for higher-speed charging, or use a USB‑A port in cars, older chargers, and office hubs—no cable swapping.

It supports PD 3.0 and QC 3.0 with up to 65W max output (device/adapter dependent) and includes an E‑Mark chip for safer power negotiation. Need to move files too? It supports up to 480Mbps data sync for everyday transfers. Built for daily carry and rough use, this 1.2m cable is ideal for commuters, students, and frequent flyers who want fast, reliable charging without carrying three different cables.

features: True 4‑in‑1 versatility: USB‑C or USB‑A input connects to USB‑C or Lightning output, covering most phones, tablets, and accessories with one cable.
Up to 65W fast charging (adapter/device dependent): Ideal for PD-supported USB‑C phones, iPads and many USB‑C laptops when used with a compatible PD charger.
PD 3.0 + QC 3.0 support: Works with common fast-charging standards for quicker top-ups across brands.
E‑Mark smart chip safety: Helps negotiate the right power delivery and improves charging stability, reducing risk from mismatched power.
480Mbps data sync: Suitable for everyday file transfers and syncing (USB 2.0 speed).
Travel-friendly 1.2m length: Comfortable reach for desks, bedside charging, and car use without excess cable clutter.
Durable daily-carry build: Made to handle regular plugging, unplugging, and bag carry with less wear.

faq.answer: It has two inputs (USB-A and USB-C) and two outputs (USB-C and Lightning). That means it can plug into old USB-A chargers or modern USB-C PD chargers and charge either USB-C devices or Lightning (iPhone/iPad) devices.
faq.question: What makes this a 4-in-1 charging cable?

faq.answer: 65W is the maximum supported output. You will get up to 65W only when used with a compatible USB-C PD charger and a device that can accept that power (such as many USB-C laptops). Phones will draw less based on their charging limits.
faq.question: Will it really charge at 65W?

faq.answer: Yes, for compatible USB-C laptops that support USB Power Delivery over USB-C, when you use the USB-C input with a suitable PD adapter. Laptop charging may not work from USB-A input at high wattage.
faq.question: Can I charge a laptop with this cable?

faq.answer: It can support fast charging for iPhones when you use the Lightning output with a compatible USB-C PD charger and your iPhone model supports fast charging. Speed depends on adapter and iPhone charging limits.
faq.question: Does it support iPhone fast charging?

faq.answer: This cable provides two output tips, but simultaneous dual-device charging depends on the internal wiring design and the power source. For best stability and fastest speed, charge one device at a time.
faq.question: Can I charge two devices at the same time (USB-C and Lightning together)?
